text:
harper: hey team, accepted the org invite but I only have access to a subset of private repos. Some repos show me as an "outside collaborator" and I can't view the repo settings or open certain internal-only repos.
chris: weird. did you accept the invite as a member or were you added as an outside collaborator on some repos previously?
harper: i don't recall being added anywhere before. the invite email showed "You were invited to join the redwood organization" and i clicked accept. on my profile page under the org it shows me as a member, but for two infra repos it says "outside collaborator" when I open the repo.
eva: onboarding-check: sometimes if a GitHub account was previously used as an outside collaborator (e.g., via a fork or contractor access) the org join flow doesn't retroactively convert that repo-level collaborator into a team/organization member. can you paste the repo names?
harper: repo names: redwood/infra-ops and redwood/infra-credentials. other repos like redwood/apps show up fine.
org-admin-bot: org-admin: detected mixed membership for user harper (user id 98765). Repo-level collaborator entries exist for infra-ops and infra-credentials.
chris: ok that explains it. repo-level collaborator entries override some org-level permissions until an admin removes the collaborator entry or reassigns membership. @eva can you check if the repos had an outside-collab entry for harper?
eva: checking now. Running `gh api /orgs/redwood/memberships/harper --jq '.role, .state'` to verify membership then `gh api /repos/redwood/infra-ops/collaborators/harper` to see if a collaborator record exists.
harper: thanks. i ran `gh api /user` and confirm my account is harper (harper@redwood.ai).
eva: i see an existing repo collaborator record on both infra repos tied to a legacy invite from "vendor-cleanup" project. i'll remove the repo-level collaborator and then add you to the engineering-infra team so you inherit correct permissions. doing: `gh api -X DELETE /repos/redwood/infra-ops/collaborators/harper` and same for infra-credentials, then `gh api /orgs/redwood/teams/engineering-infra/memberships/harper -X PUT`
harper: cool, thanks. will that preserve any prior review assignments?
chris: outside-collab entries can be detached from PR review history but PRs themselves remain. if you had been explicitly added as reviewer via a team, those team mappings will work once you're on the team.
eva: removed collaborator entries and added to engineering-infra. you may need to refresh the UI or re-auth in gh/VSCode.
harper: i still can't see infra-credentials in the web UI.
eva: try `gh repo view redwood/infra-credentials --json name,viewerPermission` and also sign out/in on the browser. sometimes GitHub caches repo permissions in the UI.
harper: `gh repo view redwood/infra-credentials --json name,viewerPermission` returns name: "infra-credentials", viewerPermission: "READ" now. browser still 404 until i clear cache.
chris: once you have READ, you should be able to clone and open PRs. browser 404 is a caching artifact.
harper: cloning works now `git clone git@github.com:redwood/infra-credentials.git` succeeded. thanks!
eva: note for onboarding docs: cause was a legacy repo-level outside collaborator record blocking proper team-based access after org join. fix is remove collaborator entry and add membership to the correct team. i'll add this as a checklist item: if you see mixed member/outside-collaborator behavior, ping people-ops with repo names.
harper: appreciate it — leaving a note in the onboarding doc about the symptom and the gh api commands that helped. welcome on team to the rest of us!
org-admin-bot: org-admin: resolved - collaborator records deleted, team membership granted (engineering-infra).
